benefits.en: The second version expresses the speaker’s surprise and amusement rather than merely reporting two facts.
benefits.zh: 第二個版本不只是報告兩件事，還表達說話者對巧合的驚訝和趣味。

benefits.titleEn: It Provides an Immediate Conversational Reaction
benefits.en: The expression is a ready-made response. A speaker can react immediately without creating a long explanation.
benefits.zh: 這是一個現成的對話回應。 說話者可以即時作出反應，不需要先組織一段很長的解釋。

benefits.titleEn: It Helps Welcome the Arriving Person into the Conversation
benefits.titleZh: 讓剛到場的人加入對話
benefits.en: The expression can direct everyone’s attention towards the newly arrived person.
benefits.zh: 真巧！ 我們剛剛才在討論你的想法。 這個表達可以把大家的注意力轉向剛到場的人。

examples.en: Speak of the devil! We were just discussing your idea.
examples.zh: 真巧！我們剛剛才在討論你的想法。

benefits.en: The second sentence shows that Daniel’s arrival is surprising because he was being discussed.
benefits.zh: 第二句表示 Daniel 的出現十分巧合，因為大家剛才正在談論他。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Useful for Calls and Messages
benefits.en: The speaker connects the unexpected message with the earlier conversation.
benefits.zh: 真巧！ Ava 剛剛傳訊息給我！ 說話者把突如其來的訊息與之前的對話連繫起來。

examples.en: Oh, speak of the devil—Ava has just messaged me!
examples.zh: 真巧！Ava 剛剛傳訊息給我！

benefits.titleEn: It Should Not Replace Every Statement of Surprise
benefits.titleZh: 不應取代所有表示驚訝的說法
benefits.en: The expression works only when the person has just been mentioned. What a surprise! I didn’t expect to see you here!
benefits.zh: 只有在剛剛提及某人的情況下，才適合使用這個表達。 真令人意外！ 我沒有想過會在這裏見到你！

origin.statusEn: Gradual Development; Exact First Use Uncertain
origin.statusZh: 逐漸形成；確切首次用法不明

history.en: The original warning gradually lost its serious and superstitious force. Speakers shortened the proverb and began using it humorously when an ordinary person appeared just after being mentioned.
history.zh: 原來帶有警告及迷信色彩的意思逐漸減弱。 說話者把諺語縮短，並開始在剛被提及的普通人突然出現時，以玩笑方式使用這個表達。

origin.memoryEn: In the old proverb, naming someone caused an appearance; in the modern idiom, mentioning a person is immediately followed by that person’s arrival.
origin.memoryZh: 在古老諺語中，說出名字會令對方出現；在現代慣用語中，剛提起某人，那個人便立即到來。

rules.titleZh: 規則一：使用完整固定形式

rules.titleEn: Do Not Change the Verb Form
rules.titleZh: 規則二：不要改變動詞形式
rules.en: Speaking of Daniel means changing or returning to the topic of Daniel. It does not necessarily mean that Daniel has appeared.
rules.zh: Speaking of Daniel 表示轉到或重新談及 Daniel，並不一定表示 Daniel 已經出現。

rules.titleEn: The Person Must Have Just Been Mentioned
rules.titleZh: 規則三：必須剛剛提及那個人
rules.en: Ruby walked into the room, but nobody had been talking about her. ✗ What a surprise!
rules.zh: 我們正在談 Ruby，而她剛剛走進來。 真是說到誰，誰就到！ 走進房間，但沒有人剛剛談及她。 真令人意外！

examples.en: We were talking about Ruby, and she has just walked in. Speak of the devil!
examples.zh: 我們正在談 Ruby，而她剛剛走進來。真是說到誰，誰就到！

rules.titleEn: The Arrival or Contact Should Be Unexpected or Well-Timed
rules.titleZh: 規則四：對方的出現或聯絡應帶有意外或巧合
rules.en: We mentioned Ethan, and he immediately called. We invited Ethan to arrive at exactly three o’clock, and he arrived at three o’clock. A completely planned arrival does not usually create the same amusing coincidence.
rules.zh: 我們剛提起 Ethan，他便立即來電。 我們請 Ethan 準時三時到達，而他亦在三時到達。 完全按計劃發生的到達，一般不會形成相同的有趣巧合。

rules.titleEn: Use It Mainly for a Person
rules.en: We were talking about Chloe, and Chloe appeared. We were discussing rain, and it started raining. ✗ Some speakers may extend the expression to things or events, but this exercise teaches only the clear person-related meaning.
rules.zh: 我們正在談 Chloe，而 Chloe 出現了。 我們正在談下雨，而天便開始下雨。 部分說話者可能把這個表達延伸至事物或事件，但本練習只教授與人物有關的清楚用法。

rules.titleZh: 規則六：Here he is 是可選部分
rules.en: Here he is identifies the person. It is not part of the fixed idiom.
rules.zh: 用來指出出現的是誰，並不是固定慣用語的一部分。

rules.titleZh: 規則七：話語標記是可選部分
rules.en: The fixed target remains speak of the devil.
rules.zh: 固定目標仍然只是 speak of the devil。

rules.titleZh: 規則八：保留人物及事件
rules.en: The person being discussed and the person appearing must match.
rules.zh: 被談及的人與出現的人必須相同。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Make It a Real Insult
rules.titleZh: 規則九：不要把它變成真正的侮辱
rules.en: The second example changes the expression from a playful reaction into a personal attack.
rules.zh: 真巧！ 我們剛剛才在談你。 說到魔鬼。 你真的很邪惡。 第二個例子把輕鬆反應變成了人身攻擊。

examples.en: Speak of the devil! We were just talking about you.
examples.zh: 真巧！我們剛剛才在談你。

examples.en: Speak of the devil. You really are evil. ✗
examples.zh: 說到魔鬼。你真的很邪惡。

rules.titleEn: Be Careful in Formal or Sensitive Situations
rules.titleZh: 規則十：在正式或敏感場合小心使用
rules.en: formal letters; official reports; serious religious discussions; conversations in which the arriving person may misunderstand the joke.
rules.zh: 在正式信件、官方報告、嚴肅宗教討論，以及對方可能誤解玩笑的情況中，應避免使用。

rules.titleEn: “Talk of the Devil” Is a Real Variant but Not This Exercise’s Target
rules.en: Collins notes that talk of the devil is especially associated with British English. speak of the devil
rules.zh: Talk of the devil 是真實變體，但不是本練習的目標字典同時收錄 speak of the devil 和 talk of the devil，而 Collins 指出 talk of the devil 特別常見於英式英語。 不過，本練習中的所有答案都必須使用 speak。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use the Full Historical Proverb in the Answers
rules.titleZh: 規則十二：答案不要使用完整歷史諺語
rules.en: The historical proverb helps explain the origin, but the shorter modern formula is the target of this exercise.
rules.zh: 完整歷史諺語有助解釋來源，但本練習的目標是較短的現代公式。
